tasks.short: Advise passengers to stay seated and orderly on the bus.

steps.what: Notice passengers who are not seated or not orderly.
Advise those passengers to be seated and orderly.

tasks.design: The driver notices who is not seated or not orderly and tells those passengers to sit and stay orderly. No announcement is played and no alert is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The advice depends on who is standing or arguing in the aisle at that moment.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the need to watch the cabin and speak.
tasks.still_hard: A fixed message does not see who is standing and does not settle a dispute.
tasks.human_edge: The driver judges the tone and when the bus should stop.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The driver still decides when to speak and what to say.

reach.task: Ask a standing passenger to sit before the coach moves
reach.learn: When a calm request is enough and when the vehicle should stop

evidence.claim: Telling passengers to sit and stay orderly is spoken in the cabin. A fixed message does not see who is standing.

assumptions: No recorded announcement and no alert is part of this design, so neither needs a step.
Watching the cabin and speaking both stay at full time because no mechanism shortens either step.
No system is added, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this operator already plays a safety announcement at departure.
research_questions: On a full intercity coach, how often does the driver repeat the seated-and-orderly advice after departure?

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The driver still watches the cabin and still tells passengers to sit. A quiet trip and a disputed aisle both keep that time, so the saving is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record cash receipts, ticket fares and the trip log.

steps.what: Count cash receipts and list the unsold tickets.
Note ticket fares the ticket system did not store.
Fill the fare sheet in the ticket system from stored fares.
Check each fare line against the cash receipts total.
Confirm the fare sheet and the day's log book.
File the confirmed fare sheet in the ticket system.
File the tachograph archive as the log book record.

tasks.design: The driver counts cash receipts and notes any ticket fare the ticket system did not store. The {OTHER} ticket system fills a fare sheet from those figures and from the fares it already stored, and a separate step files that sheet only after she confirms it. The {OTHER} tachograph archive files the day's hours as the log on the same confirmation, with nothing posted to the {ERP} and no driving-time alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash fares and the hours sat in a book in the cab until someone copied the tachograph card at the depot.
tasks.enabler_now: The ticket system already stores card fares, and a tachograph archive can hold the day file without the driver retyping the hours.
tasks.still_hard: Cash taken on the bus, a card the reader rejected, and a download that does not arrive still need the driver.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which cash total is real when the count and a fare line disagree.
tasks.altitude: She stops copying stored fares and hours. She still counts the cash, checks every line, and confirms the day. She does not gain a right to change a fare or a driving-time limit.

reach.task: Record the day's fares and the trip log
reach.learn: Which fares the ticket system already stored and which cash total still has to be entered

evidence.claim: Webfleet Tachograph Manager downloads and archives tachograph records remotely. This design files that kind of day record as the log. It does not add the product's remaining-driving-time alert.
Regulation 561/2006 limits driving hours and breaks, and those limits are checked from tachograph records. Filing the day record does not decide the hours.
Dutch works-council statute article 27 requires consent for systems that record worker location and behaviour. This hours file is that kind of record.
EU AI Act Annex III point 4(b) covers scoring workers or allocating tasks from behaviour. This fare sheet and this log are records, not scores.
France's CNIL fined Amazon France Logistique 32 million euros in December 2023 for scanner indicators of exact idle time. This design does not record idle-time scores.
Copying a fare the ticket system already stored is clerical. Counting cash and noting a fare the system missed stay with the driver. No measured bus-log result is used as this operator's saving.

assumptions: s1 produces the cash total and the unsold-ticket count. s3 copies those figures and does not invent a cash amount.

The ticket system produces each stored fare with ticket id, amount, payment type and time. The driver does not retype those lines. If the export is missing, she writes the fare in s2 and the fill copies only that line.

The tachograph produces the driver card id, the vehicle id, driving start, driving end, break minutes and the two odometer readings. s7 files that file. If the download fails, s7 does not run and she writes the hours by hand, which is why the low end of the range is small.
s4 accepts a line only when its amount is a receipt she counted or an exception she noted. A matching ticket id is not enough.
s5 is the confirmation. s6 files the fare sheet and s7 files the hours log only after that confirmation. A later change voids it.
The fare sheet is not posted to finance. The hours file raises no driving-time alert and is not a score of the driver.

Inserting the driver card is part of driving, outside this task. Three hours per 100 baseline hours cover a failed download and a new fare type. Zero upkeep would be wrong because those exceptions recur.
unknowns: What share of fares on this network is cash rather than a card or a prepaid ticket.
Whether the tachograph file already reaches the depot without the driver copying the hours.
research_questions: On a normal week, how many fare lines does she write because the ticket system has no record?
How many shifts end with a tachograph download she cannot see before she leaves?

already_counted.description: Time in the fare-line check for a line that does not match her cash total or her exception note.

incremental.description: Repeat a tachograph download that failed and add a new fare type to the sheet map.

approvals.approved_version: confirmed fare sheet she accepted in s5
confirmed tachograph day she accepted in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a card-paid intercity day the ticket system already holds the fares and the tachograph file replaces the handwritten log, but she still counts the cash and checks every line, so the high stays near a quarter of the task. On a cash charter, or when the download fails, she writes the fares or the hours herself, so the low stays under a tenth. Three hours of upkeep per 100 baseline hours are already off the net. No vendor timing figure is used.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read maps and plan the bus routes.

steps.what: Read the day's maps and the stop list for the routes.
Plan the bus routes when the map leaves a choice.

tasks.design: The driver reads the day's maps and the stop list, and chooses the path when the timetable does not fix it. No route sheet is filled and no off-route alert is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: A diversion depends on the road in front of the coach and on the stops still to serve.
tasks.enabler_now: A navigation screen can show a map, but it does not choose a safe path for a full coach.
tasks.still_hard: Low bridges, weight limits and a passenger who must be set down are not on a generic map.
tasks.human_edge: The driver knows which roads a coach can take.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The driver still reads the map and still chooses the path.

reach.task: Choose a diversion when the usual road is closed
reach.learn: Which roads a full coach cannot take

evidence.claim: Choosing a coach path is a judgement about the vehicle and the stops still to serve. A generic map does not make that choice.

assumptions: No route sheet is filled and no off-route alert is sent, so neither needs a step.
Reading the map and choosing the path both stay at full time. A screen that shows the same map does not shorten either step.
The published timetable is produced by the planner outside this task. The driver only reads it.
No system is added, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether charters, rather than the published route, are a large share of this driver's week.
research_questions: How often a closure forces this driver to pick a path that is not on the timetable?

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The driver still reads the day's maps and still chooses the path when the timetable does not fix it. A routine route and a closure both keep that time, so the saving is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still advises passengers and still chooses the path from the map. On the fare sheet and the log she counts the cash, checks the lines and confirms the day, and she no longer copies stored fares or hours.
reach: Shuttle driver: record a day's fares and trip log, and learn which figures the ticket system and the tachograph already hold.
skills_to_grow: Spot a fare line that is not in her cash count or her exception note.
Refuse a log file when the tachograph day does not match the trips she drove.
role.ambitious_version: Every regular route closes its fare sheet and its hours log before she leaves the depot, with the cash and the missed tickets still in her own count. Charters and diversions stay her call.
